EU/UK carbon regulation raising ferry costs (EU maritime ETS live 2024). Modal shift to rail is secular tailwind accelerating. EES creates short-term uncertainty but long-term security benefit.

nodes.label: Q2: Internal change forces?
nodes.summary: Moderate. CEO Leriche executing CMD targets (€1bn EBITDA 2030). New dividend policy (€0.80 rising to €1.00). Capex elevated at €170-220m/year. Not transformative internal change — custodial management of monopoly asset. ESA maintains Triaging rating.

nodes.label: TC: Sufficient base (to build a strong case on)?
nodes.summary: ESA upgrades from B-. Exceptional base confirmed at ESA depth. Natural monopoly, Treaty of Canterbury, 2086 concession, 50.4% EBITDA margins, irreplaceable fixed-link infrastructure. One of the strongest competitive moats in European equities — now confirmed with deeper competitive analysis.

nodes.label: Q3: Absence of external headwinds?
nodes.summary: No — headwinds present and confirmed at ESA. EES border implementation (Apr-Sep 2026). Truck shuttle volumes declining (-5.3%). UK-EU trade structurally lower post-Brexit. ElecLink spread compression. ESA adds: Iran-driven energy costs are net positive (ferry competitive disadvantage) but reduce total cross-Channel demand.

nodes.label: Q4: (Well-invested base?)
nodes.summary: Capex elevated at €170-220m/year through 2032 — management investing in tunnel infrastructure, terminal upgrades, capacity expansion. Well-maintained asset confirmed at ESA. Capex intensity is high relative to FCF.

nodes.label: Q5: Thesis congruency with past/present?
nodes.summary: ESA upgrades from B-. Strong congruency confirmed. Channel Tunnel has been a toll road asset since opening. HSR growth thesis is continuation of existing trend (Eurostar pax records). Monopoly economics consistent for 30+ years. ESA adds: historical pattern of new operators (Eurostar evolution) validates future HSR entry model.

nodes.label: Q6: Large CfC/mispricing?
nodes.summary: Limited. 33x P/E already prices in monopoly premium and growth expectations. ESA deepens: market may under-appreciate HSR volume uplift at >90% incremental margins, but valuation leaves little room for error. Mispricing is modest not large.

nodes.label: Q7: Low trading multiple?
nodes.summary: No. 33x P/E is premium to infrastructure peers (Vinci 16.7x, Eiffage 15x, Aena 16.9x). ESA adds: EV/EBITDA ~12-14x is less extreme but still not 'low'. Multiple reflects monopoly + concession but is not cheap by any standard.

nodes.label: Q3: Is the modelling gap structural or one-off?

nodes.label: TC: Idiosyncratic, exogenous inflection?

nodes.label: A1: Big demand change-driven EPSU or EPT?

nodes.label: Q2: Does the company hold a dominant competitive position?

nodes.label: Q3: Is the business model one-to-many scalable?

nodes.label: Q4: Is the market an oligopoly (structure AND behaviour)?
nodes.summary: Cross-Channel market is oligopoly: Getlink (tunnel), DFDS/P&O/Irish Ferries (ferries), airlines. Getlink is price leader on speed and reliability. ESA adds: ferry operators face fleet renewal decisions by 2028-30 — some capacity rationalisation possible.

nodes.label: Q5: Is there fixed cost leverage for margin expansion?
nodes.summary: Exceptional and confirmed at ESA. Tunnel infrastructure is almost entirely fixed cost. Incremental shuttle or train generates >90% EBITDA margin. Key structural advantage — volume growth = near-pure profit growth. ESA quantifies: 10m additional HSR pax = ~€100-150m incremental EBITDA.

nodes.summary: Yes. Passenger/freight volumes -> tunnel utilisation -> toll/path fee revenue -> EBITDA at >90% incremental margin. ElecLink: GB-FR spread -> interconnector revenue. All observable. Confirmed at ESA.
